title: Inbound Event Normalizer and Flexible Gate for Console Usage
creator: Marisol Vega
description: Goal: build a lightweight, extensible normalization and gating layer for Console usage events that sits between the HTTP ingest endpoint and the long-term analytics pipeline. It should: 1) accept multiple historical event shapes, 2) apply deterministic normalizations (field renames, type coercions, computed fields), 3) validate against a configurable tenant policy (reject / repair / soft-accept), 4) emit structured validation telemetry and repair diffs, and 5) support progressive rollout (shadow -> canary -> enforce).
acceptance_criteria: New normalizer runs in shadow mode for 100% of ingest traffic with zero rejects and emits validation metrics within console-analytics namespace
Canary rollout to 5% with policy=repair shows <=1% user-visible errors over 48h
Normalization latency p50 < 6ms, p95 < 25ms added to ingest path (measured end-to-end)
All repair operations are reversible and logged to the repair-diffs topic for audit
Feature flag controls: shadow, canary-percent, global-policy, per-tenant override
comments: 2026-02-18 — Marisol Vega: Initial spike complete. Prototyped a normalization function that covers 5 common legacy shapes and a small rule language for field mappings. Benchmarks in the spike show ~3.8ms p50 for pure CPU normalization on our test toy (x86, 2 cores). Next: integrate with the actual ingest path and measure realistic amplification.

2026-02-23 — Daniel Kim: Design review notes: prefer deterministic, idempotent repairs (no random fills) and include a source_version header so downstream can correlate raw -> normalized. Suggested adding a compact schema-version header to each message and fallback to raw-archive S3 when shape is unknown.

2026-02-26 — Product (Asha Patel): Confirmed required repair behaviors for fields used by billing: timestamp normalization must be strict; if repair cannot resolve timezone, mark as soft-accept and tag for manual review. Asked for a daily report of repaired billing-related events.

2026-03-01 — Daniel Kim: Implemented per-tenant policy flag (global default: repair). Added metrics: validation.result (accepted|repaired|rejected|soft_accept), validation.rule_id, normalization_latency_ms. Pushed a feature branch and opened PR #1245.

2026-03-04 — Observability (Liam O'Connor): We added a new trace span name 'ingest.normalizer' and dashboards: 'Normalizer - Validation Rates' and 'Normalizer - Latencies'. Initial smoke shows a 0.7% repaired rate on test traffic containing legacy agents.

2026-03-05 — Security (Nina Rao): Quick review: normalizer must not copy PII into logs or repair-diffs topic unredacted. Action: strip email and api_key-like fields from debug outputs; store repair diffs in encrypted topic. Created follow-up ENG-96700 for encryption-at-rest verification.

2026-03-05 — Daniel Kim: Working plan: deploy normalizer as a sidecar in the ingest service (low-risk, can be toggled by feature-flag). Shadow mode will run for 7 days; if metrics stable, canary at 5% for 48h, then promote to 25% and evaluate. Fallback: on increased rejection rate >0.5% of overall peak, auto-disable normalize and fallback to raw-archive to avoid data loss. Documented rollback steps in Confluence link above.
